name: Jodrell Bank Observatory
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: Rising from the Cheshire countryside in northwest England, Jodrell Bank is a working radio astronomy observatory founded in 1945 by Bernard Lovell. Its centrepiece, the 76-metre Lovell Telescope, is the world's third largest steerable dish and tracked spacecraft during the Space Race. Visitors can see the giant white bowl turning against the fields, alongside smaller telescopes and the original control building.
